chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (blessings of God upon him) said: The testimony of women is not valid regarding the crescent moon, and it is not valid except the testimony of two just men.

key_terms.الشهادة: Legal testimony; in Islamic law, specific conditions must be met for testimony to be accepted
key_terms.الهلال: The crescent moon; its sighting marks the beginning of Islamic lunar months, especially Ramadan
key_terms.عدلين: Two just/upright witnesses; 'adl (justice/uprightness) is a specific legal qualification for witnesses
key_terms.لا تجوز: Is not permitted/valid; a standard legal formulation indicating prohibition or invalidity

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of women valid for crescent moon sighting in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits a ruling attributed to Imam Ali, the Commander of the Faithful, establishing that the sighting of the crescent moon — which determines the beginning of Islamic months such as Ramadan — cannot be established by the testimony of women alone. The ruling requires the testimony of two just ('adil) men. This reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential position on the standards of testimony for religious calendar determinations, a topic closely tied to the obligation of fasting and the performance of religious rites.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said;
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The testimony of the women is not allowed regarding the new moon, and it is not allowed except for the testimony of two just men’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Testimony of women about the crescent is not admissible, only the testimony of two just witnesses is accepted.’”
